extracted.intended_audience: researchers with a PhD and organisations (universities, research institutions, businesses, SMEs) wishing to apply for MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowships under Horizon Europe
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and requirements for preparing and submitting applications to the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Postdoctoral Fellowships (European and Global). Covers applicant and host eligibility, mobility and experience rules, funding items, application steps and supporting documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective of Postdoctoral Fellowships
rubrics_metrics.description: Support researchers’ careers and foster excellence in research; targets researchers holding a PhD who wish to carry out their research activities abroad, acquire new skills and develop their careers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PFs help researchers gain experience in other countries, disciplines and non-academic sectors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of Postdoctoral Fellowships — European Postdoctoral Fellowships
rubrics_metrics.description: Open to researchers moving within Europe or coming to Europe from another part of the world to pursue their research career. Fellowships take place in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country and can last between 1 and 2 years. Researchers of any nationality can apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: European PFs must take place in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of Postdoctoral Fellowships — Global Postdoctoral Fellowships
rubrics_metrics.description: Fund mobility of researchers outside Europe. The fellowship lasts between 2 to 3 years, of which the first 1 to 2 years will be spent in a non-associated Third Country, followed by a mandatory return phase of 1 year to an organisation based in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only nationals or long-term residents of the EU Member States or Horizon Europe Associated Countries can apply for Global PFs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-term secondments
rubrics_metrics.description: Both types of fellowships may also include short-term secondments anywhere in the world during the fellowship (except during the return phase of a Global Fellowship).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secondments are allowed during the fellowship but Global Fellowships' mandatory return phase excludes secondments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-academic placement support
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers can receive additional support to carry out a placement of up to 6 months in a non-academic organisation based in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This placement needs to take place at the end of their fellowship; intended to build bridges between academic and non-academic sectors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Euratom-specific eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: For Postdoctoral Fellowships in research areas covered by the Euratom Research and Training Programme, researchers need to be nationals or long-term residents of an EU Member State or a Euratom Associated Country; the beneficiary organisation recruiting the researcher also needs to be established in an EU Member State or Euratom Associated Country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Euratom PFs have both researcher and beneficiary establishment nationality/residency requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host organisation eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Host organisations can be a university, research institution, business, SME or other organisation based in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All disciplines are eligible for Postdoctoral Fellowships, including those covered by the Euratom Programme.

rubrics_metrics.name: PhD degree requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers should have a PhD degree at the time of the deadline for applications. Applicants who have successfully defended their doctoral thesis but who have not yet formally been awarded the doctoral degree will also be considered eligible to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The key point is the defence has occurred by the deadline even if formal award paperwork is pending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum research experience (8-year rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must have a maximum of eight years experience in research, counted from the date of the award of their PhD degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Years of experience outside research and career breaks will not count towards the above maximum. For nationals or long-term residents of EU Member States or Horizon Europe Associated Countries who wish to reintegrate to Europe, years of experience in research in third countries will not be counted; detailed calculation guidance and a self-assessment tool are available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobility rules (residency/activity restriction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in the country of the beneficiary (for European Postdoctoral Fellowships), or the host organisation for the outgoing phase (for Global Postdoctoral Fellowships) for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before the call deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This residency/activity restriction is checked for eligibility at the call deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission restrictions (from 2026)
rubrics_metrics.description: As from 2026, resubmission restrictions apply for applications that received a score below 80% the previous year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants who scored below 80% in the previous year will face restrictions on resubmitting; consult call-specific documents for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seals of Excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: Will be awarded to applications with a total score equal to or higher than 85%, but which cannot be funded due to lack of budget available under the call.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seals of Excellence identify high-scoring but unfunded proposals for recognition and possible alternative funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment obligation of beneficiary
rubrics_metrics.description: The beneficiary receiving EU funding needs to recruit the researcher for the total period of the fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recruitment is a condition of funding and the beneficiary must employ the researcher for the full fellowship duration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding items covered by the EU grant
rubrics_metrics.description: The EU provides support for the recruited researcher in the form of a living allowance, a mobility allowance, and if applicable, family, long-term leave and special needs allowances. In addition, funding is provided for research, training and networking activities, management and indirect costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and host organisations should budget and justify these items in the proposal as per the call's financial rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application preparation responsibilities (researcher)
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers: prepare an application with a host organisation of your choice. If you are an experienced researcher interested in developing your own research project you can apply for Postdoctoral Fellowships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start preparing jointly with your chosen host organisation and follow the open call on the Funding and Tender Opportunities Portal.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to find a host organisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use your network; check the list of hosting offers (expressions of interest) published on Euraxess and other job portals from research institutions interested in supporting your application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offers are often in very concrete fields proposed by the host; you will often be in contact with a supervisor to develop your application and should check eligibility requirements carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host organisation responsibilities (application & if funded)
rubrics_metrics.description: As the host organisation you will be responsible for submitting the application on behalf of the researcher. If retained for funding, your organisation will be in charge of recruiting, supervising, hosting, training and where appropriate, seconding the researcher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host organisations should post hosting offers on Euraxess and other portals to attract candidates and be prepared to fulfil management and supervisory duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission timing and deadline compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The completed proposal, including all annexes, can be submitted at any time from the opening date of the chosen call and should be submitted by the specified submission deadline of the chosen call.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Funding and Tender Opportunities Portal and call-specific deadlines; late submissions risk exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Call-specific documents and tools to consult
rubrics_metrics.description: All relevant documents are available for each call on the Funding and Tender Opportunities Portal, including MSCA work programme and general annexes, guide for applicants, specific FAQs, application and evaluation forms, guidelines on the calculation of 8-years research experience, and a self-assessment tool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the call page for the application and evaluation process, and contact points for further guidance; national/regional ERA/NCPs and the European Research Executive Agency may provide additional support.
